newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Jan-Sept current account gap 2.53 pct/GDP.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Jan-Sept current account gap 2.53 pct/GDP.

text.p: Brazil's January-September current account deficit stood at $13.5 billion, or 2.53 percent of gross domestic product, down from 2.83 percent of GDP in the January-August period, the Central Bank said.
The bank said in a statement that the 1996 result was lower than for the same period in 1995, when the nine-month current account deficit reached 2.64 percent of GDP.
The bank said that net foreign reserves in September were $57.381 billion, or $58.775 billion in the international liquidity concept which includes accounts receivable.
In August, net foreign reserves stood at $58.287 billion, or $59.643 billion according to the international liquidity concept.

The bank said that net direct foreign investment for the first nine months of 1996 was $5.804 billion, after an inflow of $347 million in September. Investment for January-September 1995 was $2.727 billion.

"The figures for January to September show that 43 percent of the current account was financed by direct foreign investment, well above the 20 percent seen in the same period of 1995," the statement said.

This week the Ministry of Industry and Commerce announced a larger than expected September trade gap of $655 million. The Central Bank said services showed a deficit of $1.8 billion in September, bringing the services deficit for the first nine months to $14.2 billion.
